Amnat Charoen is a small province that was split off from Ubon Ratchathani, and most people only pass through it on the way between Ubon and Mukdahan. But if you actually stop, you'll find a quiet, plain Isan town. What locals think of first is the giant Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang Buddha at the Buddhist park in the middle of town — the province's main Buddha image, visible from far away. Around the edges of town there are forest temples, sandstone outcrops like Phu Sing–Phu Pha Phueng, and wide rice fields where farming is the main way of life. The food is proper Isan: som tam, larb, river fish, and homemade fermented dishes. If you like small towns without big crowds of tourists, Amnat Charoen is a slow, easy stop with a genuine Isan feel.

The kitchen is halal-certified, so it also suits Muslim travellers.

An 83-room hotel on Ratchawithi Road with a clean, Japanese-minimalist look. Rooms have a small seating area and feel fairly spacious for the price, and it's about a 5-to-10-minute walk to the Victory Monument BTS. Reviews highlight clean, airy rooms and friendly staff. A good fit if you want a smart-looking room at a mid-range rate.

An 8-storey hotel on Ramkhamhaeng Soi 22, about a 5-minute walk to Ramkhamhaeng University. It's a Halal-certified hotel with a Muslim restaurant on site and free parking, offering fairly spacious, clean rooms at a low price. Reviewers praise the staff and the value, making it a solid pick for university visitors or Muslim travellers, though some rooms catch street noise.

An Accor 4-star hotel right next to IMPACT Muang Thong Thani, about a one-minute walk from IMPACT Arena and Challenger hall, the top-tier choice for anyone attending an event there. It has over 380 spacious rooms with white-and-wood decor, a sofa, and a minibar, plus a pool, gym, and spa. Reviews praise the large, clean rooms, the good breakfast, and being able to walk straight to the venues. Rates climb during big events. A solid pick for families and business travellers who want to be right by the halls.

An Accor budget hotel right in the middle of IMPACT Muang Thong Thani, a few minutes' walk from IMPACT Arena and Challenger hall. It's an ideal base if you're here for a trade fair or concert. It has over 500 rooms, small but new and clean, with a 24-hour bar and a breakfast buffet. Reviews praise the location next to the venues and the value, though they note rooms sell out fast on big event days and the area gets crowded then.

An all-suite five-star hotel of 34 suites on Charoen Krung Road, on the southern riverside stretch. Every suite is spacious, with a round bathtub by floor-to-ceiling windows or a private balcony. The 27th-floor rooftop has a pool and a bar with 270-degree views, plus a creative Thai restaurant, and service is personal and attentive. Best for couples or anyone marking a special occasion in a suite with a city outlook.
